title: Anthrobot trajectories fall into four movement types

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Anthrobot trajectories fall into four movement types

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Unsupervised clustering of 30-second trajectory segments from about 200 Anthrobots, described by straightness and gyration indices, yields four statistically distinct movement types: circular, linear, curvilinear and eclectic.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Self‐Organize into Discrete Movement Types

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Further investigation of these clusters reveals that each represents a distinct movement type: circular, linear, curvilinear and “eclectic” (Figure 2D).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Gumuskaya G, Srivastava P, Cooper BG, Lesser H, Semegran B, Garnier S, Levin M, “Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells”, Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany) (2024), doi:10.1002/advs.202303575; section “Results › Anthrobots Self‐Organize into Discrete Movement Types”. Scope: NHBE-derived Anthrobots in low-adhesive dishes, 5-hour time-lapse tracking

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-anthrobots-09: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.76

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The trajectory metrics and pipeline are explicit and computationally reproducible. The assertion of exactly four natural types is model-sensitive and may not be testable on the full cohort from public files.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Re-track public time-lapse videos, calculate straightness and gyration for 30-second blocks, and compare four-cluster support against alternative cluster numbers and continuous models.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Public videos may be a subset of the reported 197 bots.

Cluster count and labels depend on preprocessing and model choice.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.64
analysis feasibility: 0.84
data existence: 0.7
operationalizability: 0.95
discriminating power: 0.7

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Straightness, gyration and a cluster-number criterion are a fully specified reanalysis, and they would separate discrete types from a continuum if the tracks existed. The paper keeps those coordinates on request. Watching representative clips does not rerun the clustering, so the four-type partition is not resolvable from open data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Recompute straightness and gyration on the 30-second segments from the roughly 200 tracked bots and repeat the unsupervised clustering under the original and under alternative cluster counts. Four groups that align with circular, linear, curvilinear and mixed paths, and that are preferred by a stability criterion, would support discrete types; a continuous cloud or a different preferred count would refute four types.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Trajectory coordinates for the 200 bots are not public.

Four clusters can be imposed by the choice of k and by the two indices.

Example videos show one bot of each narrated type, not the sample used for clustering.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.2
data adequacy: 0.14
operationalizability: 0.84
data existence: 0.16
discriminating power: 0.4
